purpose: Recheck the staged Open WebUI security fix and upgrade/rollback behavior without touching production.

checked: upstream version and source revision labels
the DOCX and disabled-role checks each use the exact candidate image identity

positive_control.finding: DOCX embedded script executed in about:srcdoc, stole the separately signed-in household user token, read that user’s private canary file, and left one unsafe javascript link

coverage: private chat completion, persistence, restart persistence, and cross-user denial
Channels creation, membership, shared post, persistence, and role boundaries
streamed model response persisted in the channel timeline
candidate HADES theme and upload assets match their source
authenticated file upload and owner read-back with household isolation
LDAP first-login role behavior in both owner-first and household-first orders
subject separation and role persistence after restart and fresh login
existing token denied and chat endpoint returns 401 after role revocation

upgrade_checks: synthetic local-signup owner and household accounts (LDAP identity migration is not covered)
populated_upgrade_and_rollback.rollback_result: full synthetic application-data archive restored to 0.11.1 with identities, chat, channel access, private-chat/file isolation, DOCX bytes, and SQLite integrity preserved

scope.docx_preview_actor_scope: Synthetic owner shared a malicious DOCX chat with a separate household account through an explicit read grant; the household account cloned the shared chat and previewed the attachment. On the 0.11.1 positive control, same-origin script read the household session token and used it to retrieve a separately owned private text canary. The exact pinned 0.11.4 candidate blocked execution and retrieval.
scope.nyx_review: Earlier review accepted the staging result but flagged the missing full cross-user exploit flow; this follow-up closes that staging proof gap. Production hold remains: exact production backup/cutover and direct owner acceptance are still unproven.
